title: Payment Arrangement Reinstatement of a Defaulted Plan
content:
# Payment Arrangement Reinstatement of a Defaulted Plan

## Clauses in force

1. A defaulted Payment Arrangement plan may be reinstated only where the kind allows reinstatement (its reinstatements allowed is above zero) and the plan's reinstatements so far — the re-deferrals booked on it at reinstatement over its whole life — are below that number.
2. Reinstatement must be requested no later than the reinstatement window after the date the plan defaulted. The window is counted in calendar days from the day after the default date, and a request on the last day is accepted. The default date is the plan's latest status date, the date it moved to defaulted status.
3. A plan that cannot be reinstated stays defaulted, and its balance stays due on the service agreement.

## Retired clauses

- The former clause that before reinstatement the customer must have paid the kind's share of all installments recorded as missed, through payments posted to the service agreement after the default, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The former clause that on reinstatement the plan returns to active, the missed-installment count restarts from zero, the returned balance is deferred into the plan again, and the remaining installments keep their numbers and amounts, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Window cases (hypothetical, window of 30 days)

| Plan defaulted on | First day of the window | Last day of the window | Request made on | Inside the window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | August 2 | Yes — the last day is accepted |
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | August 3 | No |
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | July 3 | Yes — no later than the last day |

## Points of judgement

- A kind that allows no reinstatement keeps a defaulted plan defaulted.
- A plan already reinstated once, on a kind allowing one reinstatement, cannot be reinstated again.
